name: Fail-Safe vs Fault-Tolerant
title: Fail-Safe vs Fault-Tolerant
description: Fail-safe means failures lead to a safe state (train brakes apply when power is lost). Fault-tolerant means the system keeps working through faults (aircraft flies on with an engine out). Different goals, different designs.
how_it_works: Choose per function: fail-safe where stopping safely is acceptable, fault-tolerant where continued operation is required. Some functions need both at different fault levels.
key_points: Choose per function by mission need.
requirements: Defined failure modes to handle; required behavior under faults (safe state or continued operation); fault assumptions.
standards: Fault tolerance and safety design practice; redundancy standards by industry.
citations: Avizienis et al. - fundamental concepts of dependable computing.
IEC 61508 architectural constraints and fault tolerance.

name: Redundancy Basics

how_it_works: Add redundancy to critical functions, ensure independence (no shared failure modes), and include fault detection with switchover. Test the redundant path - untested backup is hope.
requirements: Defined failure modes to handle; required behavior under faults (safe state or continued operation); fault assumptions.
standards: Fault tolerance and safety design practice; redundancy standards by industry.

key_points: Recovery verified for correctness and timing.
